name: Eduardo Cruickshank
detail: Assembly president who proposed a one-off solidarity tax on large bank deposits to President Alvarado in 2020 (Observador, 7 Oct 2020); Wikidata Q96104614 records his death on 2025-03-05.

name: Expediente 24.206 (Frente Amplio)
detail: Reintroduces a tax on extraterritorial passive income to fund Avancemos scholarships; an income tax, rejected in committee in 2026.

name: Paola Vega bill (June 2020)
detail: Her own bill raises income-tax rates on salaries above CRC 4.3 million and on companies with net income above CRC 1,000 million; her wealth-levy support is recorded separately.

name: Francisco Robles, Juliana Martínez and the other signers of the open letter to 100 business owners (UCR researchers, April 2020)
detail: The letter asks the richest businesspeople to contribute to a solidarity fund; the article does not show a tax call by the signers. The economist Lorenzo Ramírez, quoted in the same article, is recorded.

name: Observatorio Económico y Social, Universidad Nacional
detail: March 2020 proposals raise taxes on capital income and income-tax rates above CRC 22 million a year; no wealth tax.

name: Ley 8683 (impuesto solidario a las viviendas de lujo)
detail: Property tax on luxury homes; not a tax on net wealth.

name: Jonathan Acuña (Frente Amplio)
detail: Said the group would back reformulating existing taxes to make them more progressive, not new taxes; no wealth tax named (Observador, undated search snippet only, page not opened).

name: Ariel Robles Barrantes
detail: Frente Amplio presidential candidate 2026; his programme proposes an inheritance tax above US$3 million and he said no new taxes would be created; no tax on net wealth shown.

name: David Hernández Brenes
detail: Partido de la Clase Trabajadora candidate 2026; asked for more progressive taxes on those with billions of colones, without naming a tax on wealth.

name: Laura Fernández
detail: President since May 2026; promised neither to raise nor to create taxes.
